title: Julia Tao
text:
I am an aerospace engineer and MIT Ph.D. specializing in aircraft design, alternative-fuel safety architectures, and flight vehicle testing. My work bridges multi-physics analytical modeling with hands-on hardware prototyping, manufacturing, and testing.
Based in the Greater Boston area (Medford, MA), I am seeking full-time roles focused on aerospace R&D, systems engineering, and design/test engineering, especially those with a strong hands-on or physical hardware component.

title: Firefly: Small Deployable Micro-UAV
text:
As part of my S.M. research at the MIT International Center for Air Transportation, I led the design and development of the stability and control system for Firefly—a deployable micro-UAV powered by a slow-burning solid rocket motor.
The primary engineering challenge involved engineering a reliable deployment mechanism that could transition seamlessly from a compact stowed rocket configuration to a stable flying wing/tail architecture under changing vehicle static margin.

As part of my S.M. research at the MIT International Center for Air Transportation, I led the design and development of the stability and control system for Firefly—a deployable micro-UAV powered by a slow-burning solid rocket motor.
The primary engineering challenge involved engineering a reliable deployment mechanism that could transition seamlessly from a compact stowed rocket configuration to a stable flying wing/tail architecture under changing vehicle static margin.

title: Firefly: Small Deployable Micro-UAV
text:
Key Contributions & Technical Highlights

Folding-Tail Mechanism: Designed a pull-spring-actuated folding tail utilizing an oblique hinge that serves as both the physical deployment axis and the aerodynamic actuation axis.
Rapid Prototyping: Iterated rapidly through multiple 3D-printable vehicle iterations to test hinge mechanics, deployment reliability, and structural integrity.
Wind-Tunnel Testing: Built a custom pitch-balance test setup to experimentally evaluate longitudinal stability and controllability across various angles of attack.
Flight Testing: Conducted unpowered drop tests deployed from a quadcopter platform to capture real-world flight dynamics data.
Validation: Correlated experimental wind-tunnel and drop-test data against analytical predictions generated via AVL (Athena Vortex Lattice) vortex-lattice methods.
